# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

# glob — file search
Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

# grep — content search
Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.

Documentation lookup is unnecessary when the request is purely about code in the workspace and does not require IBM product knowledge.

# Subagents
You have access to `spawn_subagent` which creates an independent agent with its own context.

**Default: do the work yourself.** Most tasks are faster and cheaper without a subagent.
Only consider a subagent when ALL of these apply:
- The task is clearly self-contained and only needs a summary back

- You cannot accomplish it with 1-2 direct tool calls

Available types:

**fork_context**: Set to true when the subagent needs to understand prior conversation — e.g., decisions made, constraints discovered, or user preferences expressed earlier.

Do NOT use subagents for:

# create_chart — chart output
Use the `create_chart` tool when the user asks for a chart or data visualisation.

## How it works
Call the tool with:
- `type`: one of LineChart | BarChart | PieChart | ScatterChart | RadarChart | BoxplotChart
- `title`: short human-readable title for the chart tile
- `props`: a JSON string of chart-specific props

The props JSON must be valid for the chosen chart type. Do NOT wrap it in a spec fence.
Example for BarChart:
{"xAxisData":["Jan","Feb","Mar"],"series":[{"name":"Revenue","data":[4200,5800,3900]}],"title":"Monthly Revenue"}

Activate the `create-chart` skill before building props to get the full per-type prop schemas.

# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

Here's a comprehensive overview of my capabilities as **IBM Bob**:

---

## 🧠 Core Capabilities

### 1. **Agentic Chat Interface**
The primary interface for complex, multi-step development tasks. I can:
- Read files and reason across your **full codebase**
- Ask clarifying questions
- Autonomously implement features **end-to-end** across multiple files
- Edit databases and configuration files

### 2. **Modes**
Specialized personas that tailor my behavior for specific tasks. For example:
- **Plan mode** — create and review an implementation plan before coding
- **Code mode** — implement the approved plan with a focused context window
- You can also create **custom modes** for specialized workflows (e.g., product management tasks)

### 3. **Powerful Built-in Tools**
- **File access** — read and write files directly in your project
- **Run commands** — execute terminal/shell commands from within Bob
- **External tools via MCP** — extend my capabilities through the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) framework to connect to databases, APIs, and custom scripts

### 4. **Literate Coding**
Write code with AI assistance **directly inside your editor** — no need to switch to a chat window. You type instructions in plain language right where the code should go, and I generate the implementation in context, showing a diff for your review. Best for:
- Adding wrapper logic (retry, error handling, logging)
- Refactoring specific blocks
- Quick, targeted modifications

Reference specific project elements directly in conversation:
- `@/path/to/file.js` — include specific file contents

Review **every tool** I plan to use before it executes, giving you full control over my actions.

The `/init` command scans your project and generates `AGENTS.md` files — structured summaries Bob uses as **persistent context** across every conversation, so I don't need to rediscover your codebase each time.

### 8. **Code Reviews (`/review`)**
Catch potential issues before you commit your work.

### 9. **AI-Assisted Code Completion**
In-editor completions powered by AI as you type.

### 10. **Custom Rules**
Standardize my behavior with custom rules to enforce project-specific conventions, coding standards, and preferences.

- **MCP Servers** — connect me to external services (databases, APIs, scripts) for tool discovery, tool invocation, and resource access

- **IDE Integration** — real-time workspace awareness and in-editor diff viewing

data.content:
# Create Plan

Follow this structured workflow to produce a high-quality, actionable plan.

## Step 1 — Gather Requirements

Ask the user clarifying questions to fully understand the task:
- What is the goal and expected outcome?
- Are there constraints, preferences, or non-goals?
- Which parts of the codebase are likely involved?
- Any related issues or requirement documents?

Do not proceed until you have enough context to scope the work, be critical of vague intent or requirements.

## Step 2 — Code Search via Sub-Agent

Spawn a `spawn_subagent` of type `"explore"` to research the codebase. The sub-agent should:
- Locate relevant files, symbols, and patterns related to the task
- Identify existing utilities or abstractions that should be reused
- Identify existing design patterns
- Surface any constraints or conventions (e.g. patterns in similar files)

Use the sub-agent's findings to ground your plan in the actual code.

## Step 3 — Clarify Design Intention

Based on the requirements and code research:
- Always confirm your understanding of the intended design with the user
- Raise any open questions or trade-offs that need a decision
- Adjust scope if the code research revealed complexity or simplifications

Do not begin writing the plan document until design intent is confirmed.

## Step 4 — Write the Plan File

Write a structured plan to a markdown file (e.g. `{short-plan-name}-plan.md`). The plan must NOT go into low-level code detail — focus on *what* needs to happen and *why*.

The plan file must include:

### Top-Level Overview
A concise summary of the goal, scope, and approach.

### Sub-Tasks
Break the work into sub-tasks. Each sub-task must have:
- **Intent** — what this sub-task achieves and why
- **Expected Outcomes** — observable results when this sub-task is complete
- **Todo List** — ordered, specific steps to achieve the outcome
- **Relevant Context** — pointers to relevant files, symbols, or patterns
- **Status** — `[ ] pending` (updated to `[x] done` after completion)

Design each sub-task to be processed independently, one at a time, so changes stay focused and reviewable.

## Step 5 — Plan Validation

Before moving to implementation, ensure that the user has fully read the plan. Always ask the user targeted questions to verify the plan is correct and complete:
- Does this plan capture the full scope of the task?
- Are the sub-task boundaries and ordering correct?
- Is any context missing that would be needed during implementation?

Use Mermaid diagrams in chat responses where they clarify architecture or workflow, but do not place Mermaid diagrams directly in the plan file. Avoid double quotes and parentheses inside square brackets in Mermaid syntax.

Refine the plan file based on the user's answers.

## Step 6 — Implementation

Only after the user confirms the plan, recommend implementation by calling the `switch_mode` tool to `agent`.

When explaining how to implement the plan in agent mode:
- Using the `start_subtask` tool, create a new task for each subtask in the <plan-file>.
- In the prompt for the subtask make sure it reads the plan-file to gain the full context around the task.
- After each sub task is complete update the task status in the <plan-file>
- Add any context needed for the next subtask in the <plan-file>
- Wait for the user to check and ok the changes before moving on to the next subtask.

## Reminders

- Ask questions always using the "ask_followup_question" tool
- Never include information without evidence
- Don't include time estimates
Let me first explore the existing branches and any team plan documents before asking clarifying questions.

arguments.content:
# Multi-Agent Code Intelligence System — Plan

## Top-Level Overview

Build a multi-agent orchestration system on an AWS EC2 instance (Ubuntu 22.04, t3.xlarge) that:

1. **Ingests any Git repository** given a clone URL
2. **Spawns one AG2 AssistantAgent per file** for lossless, hallucination-free ingestion
3. **Orchestrates agents** inside AG2 GroupChats (orchestrator selects the next speaker dynamically) with LangGraph managing the inter-stage pipeline flow
4. **Builds a Neo4j knowledge graph** capturing all code entities, relationships, dependencies, and criticality scores
5. **Builds a ChromaDB vector store** for semantic search and embedding-based retrieval
6. **Runs a Risk Engine** that calculates blast-radius and change-impact for any file/function
7. **Runs a Code Correction Engine** that uses official language documentation (versioned) to find and fix indentation, compile, run, and logic errors
8. **Exposes all agent activity** via OpenTelemetry → Grafana + Tempo + Loki (fully visible, not background)
9. **Is fully fault-tolerant** with Redis-backed checkpoints so any failed pipeline stage can resume from its last save point
10. **Connects to external tools** via A2A protocol and MCP servers (language docs, linters, compilers, etc.)
11. **Uses CrewAI** for inter-agent critique and review flows (agents challenge each other's outputs before committing results)

The entire system runs as Docker Compose services on EC2. A thin REST API (FastAPI) acts as the user-facing entry point. All source code lives on the `arnav-branch-agents` branch.

### Framework Stack Summary

| Concern | Technology |
|---|---|
| Core agent runtime | AG2 (AutoGen v2) |
| Pipeline orchestration | LangGraph |
| Inter-agent critique | CrewAI |
| External tool protocol | MCP + A2A |
| Knowledge graph DB | Neo4j (Docker) |
| Vector store | ChromaDB (Docker) |
| Checkpointing | Redis |
| Observability | OpenTelemetry SDK → Tempo (traces) + Loki (logs) + Grafana (UI) |
| LLM backend | Gemini API (user-provided key) |
| Infrastructure | Docker Compose on EC2 t3.xlarge Ubuntu 22.04 |
| Entry point API | FastAPI |

---

## Architecture Diagram (described)

```
User → FastAPI (REST) → LangGraph Pipeline Orchestrator
         │
         ├─ Stage 1: Ingestion
         │     AgentCreator → GroupChat(FileAgents[N]) → FileAnalysis results
         │
         ├─ Stage 2: Knowledge Graph
         │     GroupChat(KGAgents) → Neo4j + ChromaDB
         │
         ├─ Stage 3: Risk Engine
         │     GroupChat(RiskAgents) → RiskReport (JSON + Neo4j edges)
         │
         └─ Stage 4: Code Correction
               GroupChat(CorrectionAgents + DocFetcherAgents) → PatchSet

All stages → OpenTelemetry → Tempo/Loki/Grafana
All stages ↔ Redis (checkpoint read/write)
GroupChats ↔ MCP servers (linters, compilers, doc fetchers)
CrewAI critique layer wraps each GroupChat output before stage exit
```

---

## Sub-Tasks

---

### Sub-Task 1 — Project Scaffold & Environment Setup

**Status:** `[ ] pending`

**Intent:**
Create the base directory structure, Python environment definition, Docker Compose skeleton, and EC2 setup scripts. This is the foundation everything else builds on.

**Expected Outcomes:**
- `agents/` directory tree created with all module stubs
- `requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml` with all dependencies pinned
- `docker-compose.yml` with service definitions for Neo4j, ChromaDB, Redis, Grafana, Tempo, Loki, and the FastAPI app
- `.env.example` updated with all required variables (GEMINI_API_KEY, NEO4J_URI, etc.)
- EC2 bootstrap script (`scripts/ec2_bootstrap.sh`) that installs Docker, Docker Compose, pulls images, and starts services
- SSH deployment script (`scripts/deploy.sh`) that syncs code and restarts containers

**Todo List:**
1. Create `agents/` directory with sub-packages: `core/`, `ingestion/`, `knowledge_graph/`, `risk_engine/`, `code_correction/`, `observability/`, `api/`, `checkpointing/`, `mcp_servers/`
2. Write `agents/requirements.txt` pinning: `pyautogen[gemini]`, `langgraph`, `langchain`, `langchain-google-genai`, `crewai`, `neo4j`, `chromadb`, `opentelemetry-sdk`, `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp`, `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `redis`, `gitpython`, `tree-sitter`, `mcp`
3. Write `agents/docker-compose.yml` with services: `neo4j`, `chroma`, `redis`, `grafana`, `tempo`, `loki`, `otel-collector`, `agent-api`
4. Update `.env.example` with: `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `NEO4J_URI`, `NEO4J_USER`, `NEO4J_PASSWORD`, `CHROMA_HOST`, `REDIS_URL`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, `REPO_WORKSPACE_DIR`
5. Write `scripts/ec2_bootstrap.sh`: install Docker CE, Docker Compose v2, clone repo, copy `.env`, run `docker compose up -d`
6. Write `scripts/deploy.sh`: rsync code over SSH, `docker compose pull`, `docker compose up -d --build`
7. Write `agents/Dockerfile` for the `agent-api` service

**Relevant Context:**
- EC2: Ubuntu 22.04, t3.xlarge (4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM)
- All secrets must go in `.env` (blocked by `.gitignore`)
- Frontend exists separately on `feature/frontend-phase1` — do not touch it

---

### Sub-Task 2 — Observability Foundation (OpenTelemetry)

**Status:** `[ ] pending`

**Intent:**
Set up the OpenTelemetry instrumentation layer before any agent code is written, so every agent action, LLM call, tool invocation, and pipeline stage transition is traced and logged from day one.

**Expected Outcomes:**
- `agents/observability/tracer.py` — singleton TracerProvider configured to export to OTLP (Tempo)
- `agents/observability/logger.py` — structured log emitter to Loki via OTLP
- `agents/observability/metrics.py` — counters/histograms for agent calls, token usage, errors
- `agents/observability/decorators.py` — `@traced_agent_call` and `@traced_pipeline_stage` decorators that wrap any function with a span
- `docker-compose.yml` includes `otel-collector`, `tempo`, `loki`, `grafana` with preconfigured datasources
- Grafana provisioning YAML files for Tempo and Loki datasources
- One example agent call visible end-to-end in Grafana after running a smoke test

**Todo List:**
1. Write `agents/observability/tracer.py` — initialize `TracerProvider` with `OTLPSpanExporter`, set as global tracer, expose `get_tracer(name)` helper
2. Write `agents/observability/logger.py` — initialize `LoggerProvider` with `OTLPLogExporter`, expose `get_logger(name)` helper
3. Write `agents/observability/metrics.py` — initialize `MeterProvider` with `OTLPMetricExporter`, expose named meters for: `agent.calls`, `agent.errors`, `llm.tokens_used`, `pipeline.stage_duration`
4. Write `agents/observability/decorators.py` — `@traced_agent_call(span_name)` and `@traced_pipeline_stage(stage_name)` that create child spans, record exceptions, and emit log records
5. Add OTel Collector config `otel-collector-config.yaml` with OTLP receiver, Tempo exporter, Loki exporter
6. Add Grafana provisioning files: `grafana/datasources/tempo.yaml`, `grafana/datasources/loki.yaml`
7. Add `grafana/dashboards/agent-pipeline.json` — pre-built dashboard showing pipeline stage spans and agent error rates
8. Write `agents/observability/__init__.py` exporting `get_tracer`, `get_logger`, `traced_agent_call`, `traced_pipeline_stage`

**Relevant Context:**
- Every subsequent sub-task MUST import from `agents/observability` and apply the decorators
- Token usage metrics feed into cost visibility on Grafana
- Loki receives structured JSON logs (include `agent_id`, `stage`, `repo_url`, `file_path` as log fields)

---

### Sub-Task 3 — Checkpointing & Fault Tolerance (Redis)

**Status:** `[ ] pending`

**Intent:**
Build the Redis-backed checkpoint system that records pipeline progress after every stage and every agent's completion, so a crashed pipeline can restart from exactly where it failed without re-processing completed work.

**Expected Outcomes:**
- `agents/checkpointing/checkpoint_store.py` — `CheckpointStore` class wrapping Redis with `save(pipeline_id, stage, state_dict)` and `load(pipeline_id, stage) -> state_dict | None`
- `agents/checkpointing/pipeline_state.py` — `PipelineState` dataclass modeling the full state of a pipeline run (repo URL, ingested files, KG status, risk status, correction status)
- LangGraph state graph uses `CheckpointStore` as its checkpointer (plugged into LangGraph's `MemorySaver` interface)
- A resume endpoint `POST /pipeline/{pipeline_id}/resume` that re-enters the graph at the failed stage

**Todo List:**
1. Write `agents/checkpointing/checkpoint_store.py` — `CheckpointStore(redis_url)` with `save`, `load`, `list_stages`, `delete` methods; keys follow pattern `pipeline:{pipeline_id}:stage:{stage_name}`
2. Write `agents/checkpointing/pipeline_state.py` — `PipelineState` dataclass with fields: `pipeline_id`, `repo_url`, `repo_local_path`, `files`, `ingestion_complete`, `kg_complete`, `risk_complete`, `correction_complete`, `error_stage`, `error_message`
3. Write `agents/checkpointing/langgraph_checkpointer.py` — adapter that implements LangGraph's `BaseCheckpointSaver` interface backed by `CheckpointStore`
4. Write `agents/checkpointing/__init__.py`

**Relevant Context:**
- `pipeline_id` = UUID generated at pipeline start, returned to user in API response
- Every LangGraph node must call `checkpoint_store.save()` on completion
- On resume, LangGraph re-reads state and skips nodes whose output is already checkpointed

---

### Sub-Task 4 — Agent Creator & GroupChat Factory

**Status:** `[ ] pending`

**Intent:**
Build the `AgentCreator` — the core factory that, given a task description and a list of file paths, dynamically instantiates the correct AG2 `AssistantAgent`/`UserProxyAgent` pairs with appropriate tools and system prompts, registers them into a `GroupChat`, and returns a ready-to-run `GroupChatManager`. This is the heart of the system.

**Expected Outcomes:**
- `agents/core/agent_creator.py` — `AgentCreator` class with `create_file_agents(files, task)`, `create_kg_agents()`, `create_risk_agents()`, `create_correction_agents(languages)` methods, each returning a `GroupChatManager`
- `agents/core/agent_registry.py` — `AgentRegistry` tracking all live agents by `pipeline_id` and `agent_id`, with start/stop/status methods
- `agents/core/tool_registry.py` — maps tool names to callable Python functions; tools can be attached to agents at creation time
- `agents/core/system_prompts.py` — versioned system prompt templates for each agent role
- One `AgentCreator.create_file_agents(["main.py", "utils.py"], "analyze")` call produces a functional GroupChat

**Todo List:**
1. Write `agents/core/system_prompts.py` — prompt templates for: `FILE_ANALYZER`, `KG_BUILDER`, `RISK_ANALYZER`, `CODE_CORRECTOR`, `DOC_FETCHER`, `ORCHESTRATOR`, `CRITIC`
2. Write `agents/core/tool_registry.py` — `ToolRegistry` with `register(name, fn, description, schema)` and `get(name)` methods; pre-register stubs for: `read_file`, `parse_ast`, `neo4j_write`, `chroma_upsert`, `fetch_official_docs`, `run_linter`, `run_compiler`
3. Write `agents/core/agent_creator.py` — `AgentCreator(llm_config, tool_registry, checkpoint_store)`:
   - `create_file_agents(files, task)` → one `AssistantAgent` per file, `UserProxyAgent` as driver, all in a `GroupChat`, `GroupChatManager` returned
   - `create_kg_agents()` → `AssistantAgent` for graph building, `AssistantAgent` for graph validation, critic, manager
   - `create_risk_agents()` → blast-radius analyst, dependency tracer, critic, manager
   - `create_correction_agents(languages)` → one agent per language version, doc-fetcher agent, critic, manager
4. Write `agents/core/agent_registry.py` — `AgentRegistry` with `register(pipeline_id, agent)`, `get_all(pipeline_id)`, `shutdown(pipeline_id)` and persists agent metadata to Redis
5. Write `agents/core/__init__.py`

**Relevant Context:**
- AG2 `GroupChat` with `speaker_selection_method="auto"` lets the orchestrator LLM pick next speaker
- Each `AssistantAgent` receives its file content injected into its system prompt at creation time (not during chat) — this is the key to avoiding hallucination
- LLM config uses Gemini: `{"model": "gemini-1.5-pro", "api_key": os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"), "api_type": "google"}`
- Tools are registered as AG2 function-call tools on the `UserProxyAgent`

### Sub-Task 5 — Repo Ingestion Stage

**Status:** `[ ] pending`

**Intent:**
Implement Stage 1 of the pipeline: clone the repo, enumerate all files, spawn one AG2 `AssistantAgent` per file, run the GroupChat analysis, and produce a structured `FileAnalysisResult` per file. Tree-sitter is used for language-aware AST parsing so agents receive structured summaries, not raw text.

- `agents/ingestion/repo_cloner.py` — `RepoCloner.clone(url, dest)` using `gitpython`
- `agents/ingestion/file_enumerator.py` — `FileEnumerator.enumerate(repo_path)` returning `[FileRecord(path, language, size, lines)]`

### Sub-Task 6 — Knowledge Graph Stage (Neo4j + ChromaDB)

**Status:** `[ ] pending`

**Intent:**
Implement Stage 2: take all `FileAnalysisResult` records from Stage 1 and have KG agents build a Neo4j property graph with nodes for files, classes, functions, modules, and imports, plus edges for calls, imports, inheritance, and composition. Also build a ChromaDB collection with embeddings for semantic search.

- `agents/knowledge_graph/neo4j_client.py` — `Neo4jClient` wrapping the official `neo4j` driver with typed `create_node`, `create_edge`, `run_cypher` methods

### Sub-Task 7 — Risk Engine Stage

**Status:** `[ ] pending`

**Intent:**
Implement Stage 3: query the knowledge graph to compute blast-radius scores, change-impact chains, and criticality rankings. A `RiskReport` JSON is produced that answers "if I change X, what breaks?".

- `agents/risk_engine/risk_report.py` — `RiskReport` dataclass with per-file and per-function risk scores + change-impact chains

1. Write `agents/risk_engine/impact_analyzer.py` — `ImpactAnalyzer(neo4j_client)` with `get_blast_radius(node_id, depth=3)` returning all transitively dependent nodes via Cypher `MATCH (n)-[:CALLS|IMPORTS*1..3]->(m)`
2. Write `agents/risk_engine/criticality_scorer.py` — `CriticalityScorer(neo4j_client)` computing: in-degree score, coupling score (cross-module edges), entropy score (number of distinct callers); normalize to 0–100 scale

### Sub-Task 9 — MCP Servers & A2A Integration

**Status:** `[ ] pending`

**Intent:**
Build the MCP server definitions and A2A protocol adapter that let agents call external tools (documentation APIs, linters, compilers, semantic search) in a standardized way. This is what makes the agent network extensible without code changes.

### Sub-Task 12 — EC2 Deployment & Smoke Test

**Status:** `[ ] pending`

**Intent:**
Deploy the complete system to EC2, verify all containers start cleanly, run a smoke test against a small public repo, and confirm traces appear in Grafana.

**Expected Outcomes:**
- EC2 instance running all Docker Compose services
- `POST /pipeline/start` with a small public repo returns a `pipeline_id`
- All four stages complete successfully
- Grafana shows traces, logs, and metrics for the run
- `GET /pipeline/{id}/report` returns a populated `RiskReport` and `PatchSet`

**Todo List:**
1. Provision EC2 t3.xlarge with Ubuntu 22.04 (via AWS Console or CLI) and note the public IP / DNS
2. Add EC2 SSH key path to `scripts/deploy.sh`; run `./scripts/ec2_bootstrap.sh` via SSH
3. Copy `.env` with real `GEMINI_API_KEY` and all service passwords to EC2 (never commit)
4. Run `./scripts/deploy.sh` to sync code and start containers
5. Verify all services healthy: `docker compose ps`
6. Run smoke test: `curl -X POST http://<ec2-ip>:8080/pipeline/start -d '{"repo_url":"https://github.com/pallets/flask", "branch":"main"}'`
7. Watch SSE stream: `curl -N http://<ec2-ip>:8080/pipeline/{id}/stream`
8. Open Grafana at `http://<ec2-ip>:3000`, confirm Tempo traces and Loki logs present
9. Run failure simulation: kill a container mid-pipeline, restart it, call `POST /pipeline/{id}/resume`, verify it continues from checkpoint
10. Document final deployment steps in `agents/DEPLOYMENT.md`

**Relevant Context:**
- EC2 security group must open ports: 8080 (API), 3000 (Grafana), 7474 (Neo4j browser — internal only), 8000 (Chroma — internal only)
- SSH key must be stored locally and referenced in `scripts/deploy.sh` only
- The smoke test uses Flask (small, well-known Python repo) to keep token costs low

---

## Design Decisions Log

| Decision | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| AG2 conversation pattern | GroupChat with `speaker_selection_method="auto"` | Dynamic multi-agent critique and debate; orchestrator LLM picks next speaker |
| Knowledge graph DB | Neo4j 5 (Docker) | Full graph DB, Cypher, native relationship traversal |
| Vector store | ChromaDB (Docker) | Python-native, self-hosted, no external cloud dependency |
| Checkpoint store | Redis | Fast key-value, pub/sub for SSE, battle-tested for pipeline state |
| Observability backend | Grafana + Tempo + Loki (Docker) | Fault-tolerant, no cloud dependency, logs + traces combined |
| LLM | Gemini 1.5 Pro via Gemini API | User-provided API key |
| Inter-agent critique | CrewAI `Crew` + `CriticAgent` | Structured review flow wrapping each GroupChat output |
| External tools | MCP servers + A2A protocol | Standardized, extensible, works with any AG2 agent |
| Repo ingestion | One agent per file | Lossless ingestion, no hallucination from context overflow |
| Pipeline orchestration | LangGraph `StateGraph` | Clear stage transitions, conditional error routing, built-in checkpointer interface |
| Infrastructure | Docker Compose on EC2 t3.xlarge | Cost-effective, fault-tolerant, easy redeploy |
| Code corrections | Versioned official docs via MCP | Corrections grounded in exact language version specs |

# Multi-Agent Code Intelligence System — Plan

## Top-Level Overview

Build a multi-agent orchestration system on an AWS EC2 instance (Ubuntu 22.04, t3.xlarge) that:

1. **Ingests any Git repository** given a clone URL
2. **Spawns one AG2 AssistantAgent per file** for lossless, hallucination-free ingestion
3. **Orchestrates agents** inside AG2 GroupChats (orchestrator selects the next speaker dynamically) with LangGraph managing the inter-stage pipeline flow
4. **Builds a Neo4j knowledge graph** capturing all code entities, relationships, dependencies, and criticality scores
5. **Builds a ChromaDB vector store** for semantic search and embedding-based retrieval
6. **Runs a Risk Engine** that calculates blast-radius and change-impact for any file/function
7. **Runs a Code Correction Engine** that uses official language documentation (versioned) to find and fix indentation, compile, run, and logic errors
8. **Exposes all agent activity** via OpenTelemetry → Grafana + Tempo + Loki (fully visible, not background)
9. **Is fully fault-tolerant** with Redis-backed checkpoints so any failed pipeline stage can resume from its last save point
10. **Connects to external tools** via A2A protocol and MCP servers (language docs, linters, compilers, etc.)
11. **Uses CrewAI** for inter-agent critique and review flows (agents challenge each other's outputs before committing results)

The entire system runs as Docker Compose services on EC2. A thin REST API (FastAPI) acts as the user-facing entry point. All source code lives on the `arnav-branch-agents` branch.

### Framework Stack Summary

| Concern | Technology |
|---|---|
| Core agent runtime | AG2 (AutoGen v2) |
| Pipeline orchestration | LangGraph |
| Inter-agent critique | CrewAI |
| External tool protocol | MCP + A2A |
| Knowledge graph DB | Neo4j (Docker) |
| Vector store | ChromaDB (Docker) |
| Checkpointing | Redis |
| Observability | OpenTelemetry SDK → Tempo (traces) + Loki (logs) + Grafana (UI) |
| LLM backend | Gemini API (user-provided key) |
| Infrastructure | Docker Compose on EC2 t3.xlarge Ubuntu 22.04 |
| Entry point API | FastAPI |

---

## Architecture Diagram (described)

```
User → FastAPI (REST) → LangGraph Pipeline Orchestrator
         │
         ├─ Stage 1: Ingestion
         │     AgentCreator → GroupChat(FileAgents[N]) → FileAnalysis results
         │
         ├─ Stage 2: Knowledge Graph
         │     GroupChat(KGAgents) → Neo4j + ChromaDB
         │
         ├─ Stage 3: Risk Engine
         │     GroupChat(RiskAgents) → RiskReport (JSON + Neo4j edges)
         │
         └─ Stage 4: Code Correction
               GroupChat(CorrectionAgents + DocFetcherAgents) → PatchSet

All stages → OpenTelemetry → Tempo/Loki/Grafana
All stages ↔ Redis (checkpoint read/write)
GroupChats ↔ MCP servers (linters, compilers, doc fetchers)
CrewAI critique layer wraps each GroupChat output before stage exit
```

---

## Sub-Tasks

---

### Sub-Task 1 — Project Scaffold & Environment Setup

**Status:** `[ ] pending`

**Intent:**
Create the base directory structure, Python environment definition, Docker Compose skeleton, and EC2 setup scripts. This is the foundation everything else builds on.

**Expected Outcomes:**
- `agents/` directory tree created with all module stubs
- `requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml` with all dependencies pinned
- `docker-compose.yml` with service definitions for Neo4j, ChromaDB, Redis, Grafana, Tempo, Loki, and the FastAPI app
- `.env.example` updated with all required variables (GEMINI_API_KEY, NEO4J_URI, etc.)
- EC2 bootstrap script (`scripts/ec2_bootstrap.sh`) that installs Docker, Docker Compose, pulls images, and starts services

## Design Decisions Log

| Decision | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| AG2 conversation pattern | GroupChat with `speaker_selection_method="auto"` | Dynamic multi-agent critique and debate; orchestrator LLM picks next speaker |
| Knowledge graph DB | Neo4j 5 (Docker) | Full graph DB, Cypher, native relationship traversal |
| Vector store | ChromaDB (Docker) | Python-native, self-hosted, no external cloud dependency |
| Checkpoint store | Redis | Fast key-value, pub/sub for SSE, battle-tested for pipeline state |
| Observability backend | Grafana + Tempo + Loki (Docker) | Fault-tolerant, no cloud dependency, logs + traces combined |
| LLM | Gemini 1.5 Pro via Gemini API | User-provided API key |
| Inter-agent critique | CrewAI `Crew` + `CriticAgent` | Structured review flow wrapping each GroupChat output |
| External tools | MCP servers + A2A protocol | Standardized, extensible, works with any AG2 agent |
| Repo ingestion | One agent per file | Lossless ingestion, no hallucination from context overflow |
| Pipeline orchestration | LangGraph `StateGraph` | Clear stage transitions, conditional error routing, built-in checkpointer interface |
| Infrastructure | Docker Compose on EC2 t3.xlarge | Cost-effective, fault-tolerant, easy redeploy |
| Code corrections | Versioned official docs via MCP | Corrections grounded in exact language version specs |

# Multi-Agent Code Intelligence System — Plan

## Top-Level Overview

Build a multi-agent orchestration system on an AWS EC2 instance (Ubuntu 22.04, t3.xlarge) that:

1. **Ingests any Git repository** given a clone URL
2. **Spawns one AG2 AssistantAgent per file** for lossless, hallucination-free ingestion
3. **Orchestrates agents** inside AG2 GroupChats (orchestrator selects the next speaker dynamically) with LangGraph managing the inter-stage pipeline flow
4. **Builds a Neo4j knowledge graph** capturing all code entities, relationships, dependencies, and criticality scores
5. **Builds a ChromaDB vector store** for semantic search and embedding-based retrieval
6. **Runs a Risk Engine** that calculates blast-radius and change-impact for any file/function
7. **Runs a Code Correction Engine** that uses official language documentation (versioned) to find and fix indentation, compile, run, and logic errors
8. **Exposes all agent activity** via OpenTelemetry → Grafana + Tempo + Loki (fully visible, not background)
9. **Is fully fault-tolerant** with Redis-backed checkpoints so any failed pipeline stage can resume from its last save point
10. **Connects to external tools** via A2A protocol and MCP servers (language docs, linters, compilers, etc.)
11. **Uses CrewAI** for inter-agent critique and review flows (agents challenge each other's outputs before committing results)

The entire system runs as Docker Compose services on EC2. A thin REST API (FastAPI) acts as the user-facing entry point. All source code lives on the `arnav-branch-agents` branch.

### Framework Stack Summary

| Concern | Technology |
|---|---|
| Core agent runtime | AG2 (AutoGen v2) |
| Pipeline orchestration | LangGraph |
| Inter-agent critique | CrewAI |
| External tool protocol | MCP + A2A |
| Knowledge graph DB | Neo4j (Docker) |
| Vector store | ChromaDB (Docker) |
| Checkpointing | Redis |
| Observability | OpenTelemetry SDK → Tempo (traces) + Loki (logs) + Grafana (UI) |
| LLM backend | Gemini API (user-provided key) |
| Infrastructure | Docker Compose on EC2 t3.xlarge Ubuntu 22.04 |
| Entry point API | FastAPI |

---

## Architecture Diagram (described)

```
User → FastAPI (REST) → LangGraph Pipeline Orchestrator
         │
         ├─ Stage 1: Ingestion
         │     AgentCreator → GroupChat(FileAgents[N]) → FileAnalysis results
         │
         ├─ Stage 2: Knowledge Graph
         │     GroupChat(KGAgents) → Neo4j + ChromaDB
         │
         ├─ Stage 3: Risk Engine
         │     GroupChat(RiskAgents) → RiskReport (JSON + Neo4j edges)
         │
         └─ Stage 4: Code Correction
               GroupChat(CorrectionAgents + DocFetcherAgents) → PatchSet

All stages → OpenTelemetry → Tempo/Loki/Grafana
All stages ↔ Redis (checkpoint read/write)
GroupChats ↔ MCP servers (linters, compilers, doc fetchers)
CrewAI critique layer wraps each GroupChat output before stage exit
```

| External tools | MCP servers + A2A protocol | Standardized, extensible, works with any AG2 agent |
| Repo ingestion | One agent per file | Lossless ingestion, no hallucination from context overflow |
| Pipeline orchestration | LangGraph `StateGraph` | Clear stage transitions, conditional error routing, built-in checkpointer interface |
| Infrastructure | Docker Compose on EC2 t3.xlarge | Cost-effective, fault-tolerant, easy redeploy |
| Code corrections | Versioned official docs via MCP | Corrections grounded in exact language version specs |

+# Multi-Agent Code Intelligence System — Plan
+
+## Top-Level Overview
+
+Build a multi-agent orchestration system on an AWS EC2 instance (Ubuntu 22.04, t3.xlarge) that:
+
+1. **Ingests any Git repository** given a clone URL
+2. **Spawns one AG2 AssistantAgent per file** for lossless, hallucination-free ingestion
+3. **Orchestrates agents** inside AG2 GroupChats (orchestrator selects the next speaker dynamically) with LangGraph managing the inter-stage pipeline flow
+4. **Builds a Neo4j knowledge graph** capturing all code entities, relationships, dependencies, and criticality scores
+5. **Builds a ChromaDB vector store** for semantic search and embedding-based retrieval
+6. **Runs a Risk Engine** that calculates blast-radius and change-impact for any file/function
+7. **Runs a Code Correction Engine** that uses official language documentation (versioned) to find and fix indentation, compile, run, and logic errors
+8. **Exposes all agent activity** via OpenTelemetry → Grafana + Tempo + Loki (fully visible, not background)
+9. **Is fully fault-tolerant** with Redis-backed checkpoints so any failed pipeline stage can resume from its last save point
+10. **Connects to external tools** via A2A protocol and MCP servers (language docs, linters, compilers, etc.)
+11. **Uses CrewAI** for inter-agent critique and review flows (agents challenge each other's outputs before committing results)
+
+The entire system runs as Docker Compose services on EC2. A thin REST API (FastAPI) acts as the user-facing entry point. All source code lives on the `arnav-branch-agents` branch.
+
+### Framework Stack Summary
+
+| Concern | Technology |
+|---|---|
+| Core agent runtime | AG2 (AutoGen v2) |
+| Pipeline orchestration | LangGraph |
+| Inter-agent critique | CrewAI |
+| External tool protocol | MCP + A2A |
+| Knowledge graph DB | Neo4j (Docker) |
+| Vector store | ChromaDB (Docker) |
+| Checkpointing | Redis |
+| Observability | OpenTelemetry SDK → Tempo (traces) + Loki (logs) + Grafana (UI) |
+| LLM backend | Gemini API (user-provided key) |
+| Infrastructure | Docker Compose on EC2 t3.xlarge Ubuntu 22.04 |
+| Entry point API | FastAPI |
+

+
+## Architecture Diagram (described)
+
+```
+User → FastAPI (REST) → LangGraph Pipeline Orchestrator
+         │
+         ├─ Stage 1: Ingestion
+         │     AgentCreator → GroupChat(FileAgents[N]) → FileAnalysis results
+         │
+         ├─ Stage 2: Knowledge Graph
+         │     GroupChat(KGAgents) → Neo4j + ChromaDB
+         │
+         ├─ Stage 3: Risk Engine
+         │     GroupChat(RiskAgents) → RiskReport (JSON + Neo4j edges)
+         │
+         └─ Stage 4: Code Correction
+               GroupChat(CorrectionAgents + DocFetcherAgents) → PatchSet
+
+All stages → OpenTelemetry → Tempo/Loki/Grafana
+All stages ↔ Redis (checkpoint read/write)
+GroupChats ↔ MCP servers (linters, compilers, doc fetchers)
+CrewAI critique layer wraps each GroupChat output before stage exit
+```

Plan written to [`agents/AGENT-SYSTEM-PLAN.md`](agents/AGENT-SYSTEM-PLAN.md). Here's the full picture before you approve it:

---

## Architecture Overview

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    User["User / Frontend UI"] -->|POST /pipeline/start| API["FastAPI :8080"]
    API --> LG["LangGraph Pipeline Orchestrator"]

    LG --> S1["Stage 1: Ingestion\nAgentCreator → N FileAgents\nGroupChat per batch"]
    S1 --> S2["Stage 2: Knowledge Graph\nKG Agents → Neo4j + ChromaDB"]
    S2 --> S3["Stage 3: Risk Engine\nRisk Agents → RiskReport JSON"]
    S3 --> S4["Stage 4: Code Correction\nCorrectorAgents + DocFetcher\nPatchSet JSON"]

    S1 & S2 & S3 & S4 -->|save state| Redis["Redis Checkpoint Store"]
    Redis -->|resume on failure| LG

    S1 & S2 & S3 & S4 -->|OTLP| OTel["OTel Collector"]
    OTel --> Tempo["Tempo traces"]
    OTel --> Loki["Loki logs"]
    Tempo & Loki --> Grafana["Grafana Dashboard"]

    S2 --> Neo4j["Neo4j Graph DB"]
    S2 --> Chroma["ChromaDB Vector Store"]

    S4 -->|MCP tool calls| MCP["MCP Servers\ndocs / linter / neo4j / chroma"]
    MCP -->|A2A envelopes| A2A["A2A Adapter"]

    subgraph CrewAI["CrewAI Critique Layer"]
        C1["CriticAgent wraps each\nGroupChat output"]
    end
    S2 & S3 & S4 --> CrewAI
```

---

## The 12 Sub-Tasks at a Glance

| # | Sub-Task | What it produces |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Project Scaffold & EC2 Setup | Directory tree, Docker Compose, bootstrap + deploy scripts |
| 2 | Observability Foundation | OTel SDK, Grafana/Tempo/Loki, `@traced_*` decorators |
| 3 | Checkpointing & Fault Tolerance | Redis `CheckpointStore`, LangGraph checkpointer adapter, resume endpoint |
| 4 | Agent Creator & GroupChat Factory | `AgentCreator`, `AgentRegistry`, `ToolRegistry`, system prompts |
| 5 | Repo Ingestion Stage | Clone → enumerate → AST parse → per-file agents → `FileAnalysisResult[]` |
| 6 | Knowledge Graph Stage | Neo4j graph + ChromaDB embeddings from analysis results |
| 7 | Risk Engine Stage | Blast-radius traversal, criticality scores, `RiskReport` |
| 8 | Code Correction Stage | Versioned-doc-grounded patches, `PatchSet`, linter/compiler tools |
| 9 | MCP Servers & A2A | Docs/linter/Neo4j/Chroma MCP servers, A2A adapter |
| 10 | LangGraph Pipeline Orchestrator | `StateGraph` wiring all 4 stages, conditional error edges, resume |
| 11 | FastAPI & SSE Dashboard | REST API, SSE live stream, Grafana dashboard auto-provisioning |
| 12 | EC2 Deployment & Smoke Test | Live EC2 deploy, smoke test on Flask repo, failure recovery test |

---

## Key Design Decisions

- **AG2 GroupChat** (`speaker_selection_method="auto"`) — orchestrator LLM picks next speaker dynamically, enabling critique and debate
- **One agent per file** — injected with full file content + AST summary at creation time, eliminating context overflow hallucinations
- **LangGraph** orchestrates stage transitions; **Redis** checkpoints every stage so any failure is resumable
- **CrewAI `CriticAgent`** wraps each GroupChat output before stage exit — no unchallenged results
- **MCP servers** for docs/linters/compilers + **A2A protocol** for cross-GroupChat tool calls
- **Gemini 1.5 Pro** as the LLM backend (your API key via `.env`)
- **Grafana + Tempo + Loki** all containerized — fault-tolerant, no cloud lock-in

---

**Three questions to confirm before we switch to Agent mode and implement:**

1. **File batching** — ingestion spawns one agent per file; for a large repo (500+ files) this means many parallel GroupChats. Should we cap at a maximum of, say, 20 concurrent GroupChats (batches of 20 files each), or do you want a different concurrency limit?

2. **Frontend integration** — the `feature/frontend-phase1` branch has existing UI code. Should the FastAPI SSE endpoint and API contract be designed to connect to that existing frontend, or is it standalone for now?

3. **Scope of code correction** — should the correction stage actually apply patches (overwrite files in the cloned repo) or only propose them (return diffs for user review)? Propose-only is safer but requires a separate apply step.

1 | # Multi-Agent Code Intelligence System — Plan
2 | 
3 | ## Top-Level Overview
4 | 
5 | Build a multi-agent orchestration system on an AWS EC2 instance (Ubuntu 22.04, t3.xlarge) that:
6 | 
7 | 1. **Ingests any Git repository** given a clone URL
8 | 2. **Spawns one AG2 AssistantAgent per file** for lossless, hallucination-free ingestion
9 | 3. **Orchestrates agents** inside AG2 GroupChats (orchestrator selects the next speaker dynamically) with LangGraph managing the inter-stage pipeline flow
10 | 4. **Builds a Neo4j knowledge graph** capturing all code entities, relationships, dependencies, and criticality scores
11 | 5. **Builds a ChromaDB vector store** for semantic search and embedding-based retrieval
12 | 6. **Runs a Risk Engine** that calculates blast-radius and change-impact for any file/function
13 | 7. **Runs a Code Correction Engine** that uses official language documentation (versioned) to find and fix indentation, compile, run, and logic errors
14 | 8. **Exposes all agent activity** via OpenTelemetry → Grafana + Tempo + Loki (fully visible, not background)
15 | 9. **Is fully fault-tolerant** with Redis-backed checkpoints so any failed pipeline stage can resume from its last save point
16 | 10. **Connects to external tools** via A2A protocol and MCP servers (language docs, linters, compilers, etc.)
17 | 11. **Uses CrewAI** for inter-agent critique and review flows (agents challenge each other's outputs before committing results)
18 | 
19 | The entire system runs as Docker Compose services on EC2. A thin REST API (FastAPI) acts as the user-facing entry point. All source code lives on the `arnav-branch-agents` branch.
20 | 
21 | ### Framework Stack Summary
22 | 
23 | | Concern | Technology |
24 | |---|---|
25 | | Core agent runtime | AG2 (AutoGen v2) |
26 | | Pipeline orchestration | LangGraph |
27 | | Inter-agent critique | CrewAI |
28 | | External tool protocol | MCP + A2A |
29 | | Knowledge graph DB | Neo4j (Docker) |
30 | | Vector store | ChromaDB (Docker) |
31 | | Checkpointing | Redis |
32 | | Observability | OpenTelemetry SDK → Tempo (traces) + Loki (logs) + Grafana (UI) |
33 | | LLM backend | Gemini API (user-provided key) |
34 | | Infrastructure | Docker Compose on EC2 t3.xlarge Ubuntu 22.04 |
35 | | Entry point API | FastAPI |

23 | ## 🤖 Using AI Assistants Safely (Bob, Copilot, etc.)

25 | ### The Risk
26 | 
27 | AI assistants log your prompts and code in session history files. If you share credentials with them, those credentials may be logged!

30 | 
31 | ```
32 | ❌ BAD:  "Here's my API key: abc123xyz, help me use it"
33 | ✅ GOOD: "Help me use environment variables for my API key"
34 |

36 | ✅ GOOD: "Help me structure my .env file (I'll add credentials myself)"
37 | 
38 | ❌ BAD:  api_key = "abc123xyz"
39 | ✅ GOOD: api_key = os.getenv('API_KEY')
40 | ```

# Multi-Agent Code Intelligence System — Plan

## Top-Level Overview

Build a multi-agent orchestration system on an AWS EC2 instance (Ubuntu 22.04, t3.xlarge) that operates like a **collaborative software company** — a Decision Agent acts as the "CTO/Scrum Master", reads the repository and the user-selected mode, creates a Kanban board of work items following an Agile SDLC, and dispatches specialised AG2 agent teams to execute each work item. All outputs are surfaced to the **existing `master`-branch frontend** via a well-defined API contract — no UI code changes are made.

### Core Goals

1. **Ingest any Git repository** given a clone URL — one AG2 AssistantAgent per file for lossless ingestion
2. **Decision Agent** acts as orchestrator-in-chief: reads repo + mode → creates SDLC sprint plan → dispatches sub-agents dynamically
3. **Pipeline Modes** (user-selectable, drives Decision Agent behaviour):
   - `knowledge_graph_only` — ingest + build graph, no corrections
   - `minimal_change` — knowledge graph + low-risk targeted fixes only
   - `low_profile` — knowledge graph + risk engine + conservative corrections
   - `modernise` — full pipeline including language-version upgrades and refactors
   - `greenfield` — full pipeline + architectural redesign proposals
4. **Agile/Kanban execution** — Decision Agent maintains a Kanban board (Redis-backed) with columns: `Backlog → In Progress → Review → Done`; CrewAI critique moves cards from `In Progress → Review → Done`
5. **Knowledge Graph** (Neo4j) capturing all code entities, relationships, dependencies, criticality scores
6. **Vector Store** (ChromaDB) for semantic search and embedding-based retrieval
7. **Risk Engine** — blast-radius, change-impact chains, criticality rankings
8. **Code Correction Engine** — uses official versioned language docs via MCP; scope gated by mode
9. **Fully observable** — OpenTelemetry → Grafana + Tempo + Loki; all agent decisions visible
10. **Fully fault-tolerant** — Redis-backed checkpoints; any stage resumes from exact failure point
11. **Exposes structured API** — FastAPI contract consumed by the `master`-branch frontend (no UI changes)

### Framework Stack Summary

| Concern | Technology |
|---|---|
| Core agent runtime | AG2 (AutoGen v2) |
| Pipeline + SDLC orchestration | LangGraph |
| Agile/Kanban board state | Redis (Kanban card store) |
| Inter-agent critique / review | CrewAI |
| External tool protocol | MCP + A2A |
| Knowledge graph DB | Neo4j (Docker) |
| Vector store | ChromaDB (Docker) |
| Checkpointing | Redis |
| Observability | OpenTelemetry SDK → Tempo + Loki + Grafana |
| LLM backend | Gemini 1.5 Pro (user-provided API key) |
| Infrastructure | Docker Compose on EC2 t3.xlarge Ubuntu 22.04 |
| Entry point API | FastAPI (consumed by existing master-branch UI) |
| Frontend | Existing UI on `master` branch — NO CHANGES, API contract only |

---

## Architecture Overview (text)

```
User / existing master-branch UI
        │
        │  POST /pipeline/start  {repo_url, mode}
        ▼
   FastAPI  :8080
        │
        ▼
   Decision Agent  (LangGraph entry node)
   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  1. Reads repo metadata (languages, size)     │
   │  2. Reads selected mode                       │
   │  3. Creates SDLC sprint plan (Kanban cards)   │
   │  4. Decides which stages to run & in order    │
   └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼  (conditional on mode)
   LangGraph StateGraph
   ├─ Stage 1: Ingestion          (always runs)
   │    AgentCreator → N FileAgents in GroupChats (batches of 20)
   │    → FileAnalysisResult[] → checkpoint
   │
   ├─ Stage 2: Knowledge Graph    (all modes except none)
   │    GroupChat(KGAgents) → Neo4j + ChromaDB → checkpoint
   │
   ├─ Stage 3: Risk Engine        (modes: low_profile, modernise, greenfield)
   │    GroupChat(RiskAgents) → RiskReport JSON → checkpoint
   │
   └─ Stage 4: Code Correction    (modes: minimal_change, low_profile, modernise, greenfield)
        GroupChat(CorrectorAgents + DocFetcherAgents) → PatchSet → checkpoint
        (scope of changes gated by mode)

All stages ↔ Redis Checkpoint Store  (resume on failure)
All stages ↔ Redis Kanban Board      (Decision Agent tracks progress)
All stages → OTel Collector → Tempo / Loki / Grafana
GroupChats ↔ MCP Servers            (docs / linter / compiler / neo4j / chroma)
GroupChat outputs → CrewAI Critic   (before stage exit)
Cross-GroupChat calls via A2A adapter
```

---

## Pipeline Modes — Decision Agent Behaviour

| Mode | Ingestion | KG | Risk | Correction scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `knowledge_graph_only` | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| `minimal_change` | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | Syntax / indentation only |
| `low_profile` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Low-risk bug fixes only |
| `modernise` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Language-version upgrades + refactors |
| `greenfield` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Full redesign proposals (diff only, user applies) |

---

## Agile / Kanban SDLC Model

The Decision Agent maintains a Kanban board stored as Redis hashes. Each work item is a **KanbanCard**:

```
KanbanCard {
  card_id:     UUID
  pipeline_id: UUID
  title:       str          # e.g. "Analyse src/api/routes.py"
  stage:       str          # ingestion | knowledge_graph | risk | correction
  assignee:    str          # agent_id
  status:      Backlog | InProgress | Review | Done | Blocked
  created_at:  ISO timestamp
  updated_at:  ISO timestamp
  notes:       str          # agent output summary / critique result
}
```

Flow:
1. Decision Agent creates all cards → `Backlog`
2. AgentCreator picks cards → `InProgress`
3. Agent completes work → `Review` (triggers CrewAI Critic)
4. Critic passes → `Done`; Critic fails → `Blocked` + note added → Decision Agent re-queues

The frontend (`master` branch) polls `GET /pipeline/{id}/kanban` to display the board.

---

## Frontend API Contract (master-branch UI, no UI changes)

All endpoints return JSON. The frontend consumes these — no frontend code is written here.

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `/pipeline/start` | POST | Start pipeline: `{repo_url, branch, mode}` → `{pipeline_id}` |
| `/pipeline/{id}/resume` | POST | Resume from last checkpoint |
| `/pipeline/{id}/status` | GET | `PipelineStatus` — current stage, % complete, mode |
| `/pipeline/{id}/kanban` | GET | Full Kanban board with all cards and statuses |
| `/pipeline/{id}/report` | GET | Final `RiskReport + PatchSet + KGSummary` |
| `/pipeline/{id}/stream` | GET | SSE stream of real-time agent events |
| `/pipeline/{id}/graph` | GET | Neo4j subgraph as JSON (nodes + edges) for visualisation |
| `/pipeline/{id}/corrections` | GET | List of proposed patches (diffs), status per patch |
| `/pipeline/{id}/corrections/{patch_id}/apply` | POST | Apply a specific patch to the cloned repo |
| `/modes` | GET | List available modes with descriptions |

---

**Status:** `[ ] pending`

**Intent:**
Create the base directory structure, Python environment definition, Docker Compose skeleton, and EC2 setup scripts. This is the foundation everything else builds on.

- `agents/` directory tree with all module stubs

3. Write `agents/docker-compose.yml` with services: `neo4j`, `chroma`, `redis`, `grafana`, `tempo`, `loki`, `otel-collector`, `agent-api`, `docs-mcp`, `linter-mcp`, `neo4j-mcp`, `chroma-mcp`

### Sub-Task 2 — Observability Foundation (OpenTelemetry)

Set up the OpenTelemetry instrumentation layer first so every agent action, LLM call, tool invocation, Kanban card transition, and pipeline stage is traced and logged from day one.

## Design Decisions Log

| Decision | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| AG2 conversation pattern | GroupChat `speaker_selection_method="auto"` | Dynamic multi-agent critique; orchestrator LLM picks next speaker |
| Knowledge graph DB | Neo4j 5 (Docker) | Full graph DB, Cypher, native relationship traversal |
| Vector store | ChromaDB (Docker) | Python-native, self-hosted, no cloud dependency |
| Checkpoint store | Redis | Fast KV, pub/sub for SSE + Kanban, battle-tested |
| Kanban board | Redis-backed (same instance) | Shares infra with checkpoint store, no extra service |
| Observability | Grafana + Tempo + Loki (Docker) | Fault-tolerant, no cloud lock-in, logs + traces combined |
| LLM | Gemini 1.5 Pro | User-provided API key |
| Inter-agent critique | CrewAI Crew + CriticAgent | Structured review wrapping each GroupChat output |
| External tools | MCP servers + A2A protocol | Standardised, extensible, decoupled from agent code |
| Repo ingestion | One agent per file (batches of 20) | Lossless ingestion, no context overflow hallucination |
| Pipeline orchestration | LangGraph StateGraph | Clear stage transitions, conditional mode edges, built-in checkpointer |
| Infrastructure | Docker Compose on EC2 t3.xlarge | Cost-effective, fault-tolerant, easy redeploy |
| Mode gating | Decision Agent reads mode → ModeConfig drives stage skipping | Single source of truth for pipeline behaviour |
| Correction scope | Gated by mode; patches proposed not auto-applied | Safe by default; user applies via `/corrections/{id}/apply` |
| Frontend integration | API contract only (no UI changes) | `master`-branch UI consumes FastAPI endpoints; zero frontend coupling |
| Agile execution model | Decision Agent as Scrum Master; Kanban cards per work item | Collaborative company model; visible progress; retry on block |
| SDLC structure | Epic-per-stage; card-per-file for ingestion | Maps agent work to standard Agile artefacts |

+## Pipeline Modes — Decision Agent Behaviour
+
+| Mode | Ingestion | KG | Risk | Correction scope |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| `knowledge_graph_only` | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
+| `minimal_change` | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | Syntax / indentation only |
+| `low_profile` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Low-risk bug fixes only |
+| `modernise` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Language-version upgrades + refactors |
+| `greenfield` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Full redesign proposals (diff only, user applies) |
+
+---
+
+## Agile / Kanban SDLC Model
+
+The Decision Agent maintains a Kanban board stored as Redis hashes. Each work item is a **KanbanCard**:
+
+```
+KanbanCard {
+  card_id:     UUID
+  pipeline_id: UUID
+  title:       str          # e.g. "Analyse src/api/routes.py"
+  stage:       str          # ingestion | knowledge_graph | risk | correction
+  assignee:    str          # agent_id
+  status:      Backlog | InProgress | Review | Done | Blocked
+  created_at:  ISO timestamp
+  updated_at:  ISO timestamp
+  notes:       str          # agent output summary / critique result
+}
+```
+
+Flow:
+1. Decision Agent creates all cards → `Backlog`
+2. AgentCreator picks cards → `InProgress`
+3. Agent completes work → `Review` (triggers CrewAI Critic)
+4. Critic passes → `Done`; Critic fails → `Blocked` + note added → Decision Agent re-queues
+
+The frontend (`master` branch) polls `GET /pipeline/{id}/kanban` to display the board.
+

# Multi-Agent Code Intelligence System — Plan

## Top-Level Overview

Build a multi-agent orchestration system on an AWS EC2 instance (Ubuntu 22.04, t3.xlarge) that operates like a **collaborative software company** — a Decision Agent acts as the "CTO/Scrum Master", reads the repository and the user-selected mode, creates a Kanban board of work items following an Agile SDLC, and dispatches specialised AG2 agent teams to execute each work item. All outputs are surfaced to the **existing `master`-branch frontend** via a well-defined API contract — no UI code changes are made.

### Core Goals

1. **Ingest any Git repository** given a clone URL — one AG2 AssistantAgent per file for lossless ingestion
2. **Decision Agent** acts as orchestrator-in-chief: reads repo + mode → creates SDLC sprint plan → dispatches sub-agents dynamically
3. **Pipeline Modes** (user-selectable, drives Decision Agent behaviour):
   - `knowledge_graph_only` — ingest + build graph, no corrections
   - `minimal_change` — knowledge graph + low-risk targeted fixes only
   - `low_profile` — knowledge graph + risk engine + conservative corrections
   - `modernise` — full pipeline including language-version upgrades and refactors
   - `greenfield` — full pipeline + architectural redesign proposals
4. **Agile/Kanban execution** — Decision Agent maintains a Kanban board (Redis-backed) with columns: `Backlog → In Progress → Review → Done`; CrewAI critique moves cards from `In Progress → Review → Done`
5. **Knowledge Graph** (Neo4j) capturing all code entities, relationships, dependencies, criticality scores
6. **Vector Store** (ChromaDB) for semantic search and embedding-based retrieval
7. **Risk Engine** — blast-radius, change-impact chains, criticality rankings
8. **Code Correction Engine** — uses official versioned language docs via MCP; scope gated by mode
9. **Fully observable** — OpenTelemetry → Grafana + Tempo + Loki; all agent decisions visible
10. **Fully fault-tolerant** — Redis-backed checkpoints; any stage resumes from exact failure point
11. **Exposes structured API** — FastAPI contract consumed by the `master`-branch frontend (no UI changes)

### Framework Stack Summary

| Concern | Technology |
|---|---|
| Core agent runtime | AG2 (AutoGen v2) |
| Pipeline + SDLC orchestration | LangGraph |
| Agile/Kanban board state | Redis (Kanban card store) |
| Inter-agent critique / review | CrewAI |
| External tool protocol | MCP + A2A |
| Knowledge graph DB | Neo4j (Docker) |
| Vector store | ChromaDB (Docker) |
| Checkpointing | Redis |
| Observability | OpenTelemetry SDK → Tempo + Loki + Grafana |
| LLM backend | Gemini 1.5 Pro (user-provided API key) |
| Infrastructure | Docker Compose on EC2 t3.xlarge Ubuntu 22.04 |
| Entry point API | FastAPI (consumed by existing master-branch UI) |
| Frontend | Existing UI on `master` branch — NO CHANGES, API contract only |

---

## Architecture Overview (text)

```
User / existing master-branch UI
        │
        │  POST /pipeline/start  {repo_url, mode}
        ▼
   FastAPI  :8080
        │
        ▼
   Decision Agent  (LangGraph entry node)
   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  1. Reads repo metadata (languages, size)     │
   │  2. Reads selected mode                       │
   │  3. Creates SDLC sprint plan (Kanban cards)   │
   │  4. Decides which stages to run & in order    │
   └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │
        ▼  (conditional on mode)
   LangGraph StateGraph
   ├─ Stage 1: Ingestion          (always runs)
   │    AgentCreator → N FileAgents in GroupChats (batches of 20)
   │    → FileAnalysisResult[] → checkpoint
   │
   ├─ Stage 2: Knowledge Graph    (all modes except none)
   │    GroupChat(KGAgents) → Neo4j + ChromaDB → checkpoint
   │
   ├─ Stage 3: Risk Engine        (modes: low_profile, modernise, greenfield)
   │    GroupChat(RiskAgents) → RiskReport JSON → checkpoint
   │
   └─ Stage 4: Code Correction    (modes: minimal_change, low_profile, modernise, greenfield)
        GroupChat(CorrectorAgents + DocFetcherAgents) → PatchSet → checkpoint
        (scope of changes gated by mode)

All stages ↔ Redis Checkpoint Store  (resume on failure)
All stages ↔ Redis Kanban Board      (Decision Agent tracks progress)
All stages → OTel Collector → Tempo / Loki / Grafana
GroupChats ↔ MCP Servers            (docs / linter / compiler / neo4j / chroma)
GroupChat outputs → CrewAI Critic   (before stage exit)
Cross-GroupChat calls via A2A adapter
```

## Pipeline Modes — Decision Agent Behaviour

| Mode | Ingestion | KG | Risk | Correction scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `knowledge_graph_only` | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| `minimal_change` | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | Syntax / indentation only |
| `low_profile` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Low-risk bug fixes only |
| `modernise` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Language-version upgrades + refactors |
| `greenfield` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Full redesign proposals (diff only, user applies) |

---

## Agile / Kanban SDLC Model

The Decision Agent maintains a Kanban board stored as Redis hashes. Each work item is a **KanbanCard**:

```
KanbanCard {
  card_id:     UUID
  pipeline_id: UUID
  title:       str          # e.g. "Analyse src/api/routes.py"
  stage:       str          # ingestion | knowledge_graph | risk | correction
  assignee:    str          # agent_id
  status:      Backlog | InProgress | Review | Done | Blocked
  created_at:  ISO timestamp
  updated_at:  ISO timestamp
  notes:       str          # agent output summary / critique result
}
```

Flow:
1. Decision Agent creates all cards → `Backlog`
2. AgentCreator picks cards → `InProgress`
3. Agent completes work → `Review` (triggers CrewAI Critic)
4. Critic passes → `Done`; Critic fails → `Blocked` + note added → Decision Agent re-queues

The frontend (`master` branch) polls `GET /pipeline/{id}/kanban` to display the board.

## Frontend API Contract (master-branch UI, no UI changes)

All endpoints return JSON. The frontend consumes these — no frontend code is written here.

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `/pipeline/start` | POST | Start pipeline: `{repo_url, branch, mode}` → `{pipeline_id}` |
| `/pipeline/{id}/resume` | POST | Resume from last checkpoint |
| `/pipeline/{id}/status` | GET | `PipelineStatus` — current stage, % complete, mode |

## Design Decisions Log

| Decision | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| AG2 conversation pattern | GroupChat `speaker_selection_method="auto"` | Dynamic multi-agent critique; orchestrator LLM picks next speaker |
| Knowledge graph DB | Neo4j 5 (Docker) | Full graph DB, Cypher, native relationship traversal |
| Vector store | ChromaDB (Docker) | Python-native, self-hosted, no cloud dependency |
| Checkpoint store | Redis | Fast KV, pub/sub for SSE + Kanban, battle-tested |
| Kanban board | Redis-backed (same instance) | Shares infra with checkpoint store, no extra service |
| Observability | Grafana + Tempo + Loki (Docker) | Fault-tolerant, no cloud lock-in, logs + traces combined |
| LLM | Gemini 1.5 Pro | User-provided API key |
| Inter-agent critique | CrewAI Crew + CriticAgent | Structured review wrapping each GroupChat output |
| External tools | MCP servers + A2A protocol | Standardised, extensible, decoupled from agent code |
| Repo ingestion | One agent per file (batches of 20) | Lossless ingestion, no context overflow hallucination |
| Pipeline orchestration | LangGraph StateGraph | Clear stage transitions, conditional mode edges, built-in checkpointer |
| Infrastructure | Docker Compose on EC2 t3.xlarge | Cost-effective, fault-tolerant, easy redeploy |
| Mode gating | Decision Agent reads mode → ModeConfig drives stage skipping | Single source of truth for pipeline behaviour |
| Correction scope | Gated by mode; patches proposed not auto-applied | Safe by default; user applies via `/corrections/{id}/apply` |
| Frontend integration | API contract only (no UI changes) | `master`-branch UI consumes FastAPI endpoints; zero frontend coupling |
| Agile execution model | Decision Agent as Scrum Master; Kanban cards per work item | Collaborative company model; visible progress; retry on block |
| SDLC structure | Epic-per-stage; card-per-file for ingestion | Maps agent work to standard Agile artefacts |
